thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Tech Leads Stock-market Rally As Investors Look Past Trade Worries

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Tech Leads Stock-market Rally As Investors Look Past Trade Worries
text:
By Sara Sjolin and Anora M. Gaudiano, MarketWatch
Consumer, technology stocks lead gains on Wall Street
U.S. stocks advanced on Monday led by solid gains in the technology and consumer sectors, as traders appeared to shrug off global trade tensions and focus on favorable economic environment instead.
What are markets doing?
The Nasdaq Composite traded above its previous closing high, after rising 44 points, or 0.6%, to 7,599.
The S&P 500 was up 11 points, or 0.4%, to 2,746, with nine of its 11 sectors trading higher. Technology, consumer discretionary and consumer staples sectors led the gains, up nearly 1%.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 190 points, or 0.8%, to 24,826.
The Russell 2000 also hit an intraday high, then retreated to trade flat at 1,648.
The gains come on the heels of a strong session on Friday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stocks-poised-to-rebound-as-jobs-report-steals-focus-from-trade-wars-2018-06-01) when the Dow finished 0.9% higher, the Nasdaq Composite Index rose 1.5% and the S&P 500 booked a 1.1% gain.
What is driving the market?
Investors continued to cheer a round of solid U.S. jobs data out on Friday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-gains-223000-new-jobs-in-may-unemployment-falls-to-18-year-of-38-2018-06-01), which showed the world's largest economy in better economic health than expected. That helped spur a move back into riskier assets such as stocks, after political upheaval in Italy earlier last week sparked a flight into havens such as bonds.
The optimism over the U.S. data also helped overshadow lingering concerns over global trade on Monday. A round of trade talks between the U.S. and China broke down over the weekend with no agreement, indicating a full-on trade war between the world's two largest economies could be imminent.
Read:China warns U.S.: Trade agreements are off if tariffs are imposed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/china-warns-us-trade-agreements-are-off-if-tariffs-are-imposed-2018-06-03)
Meanwhile, finance ministers from Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the U.K. at a G-7 meeting on Saturday issued a rare rebuke to the U.S (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/other-g-7-members-issue-rare-condemnation-of-us-tariffs-2018-06-03)., expressing their "unanimous concern and disappointment" about President Donald Trump's decision to place tariffs on metals imports from his major allies.
Tariffs and trade are also likely to feature highly on the agenda when leaders of the G-7 nations -- including the U.S. -- hold talks in Canada on Friday and Saturday.
What are strategists saying?
"Retailers are doing well today because of massive upgrade by Evercore of Macy's, which said that the worst is over for the sector," said Diane Jaffee, senior portfolio manager at TCW Group.
Read:The stock market's most-loved and most-hated equities have something in common (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-what-the-stock-markets-most-loved-and-most-hated-shares-have-in-common-2018-06-04)
"Latest economic reports indicate that consumers finally have confidence and extra income to spend on big-ticket items. Really low levels of unemployment and underemployment bode well for the retail sector and the market in general," Jaffee said.
David Kelly, chief global strategist at JPMorgan Funds, said the U.S. economy is dealing with a combination of fiscal stimulus, which he likened to coffee, and a depressant in terms of trade tensions, which he compared to vodka.
"For the moment, the U.S. economy seems to be faring well on a diet of vodka and espresso. Longer term, however, a combination of excessive stimulus and protectionism domestically is a good reason for investors to make sure they have sufficient international diversification," he said, in a note.
What's on the economic calendar?
U.S. factory orders (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-factory-orders-drop-08-in-april-2018-06-04)fell by 0.8% in April, driven by a decline in commercial aircraft.
There will be no Federal Reserve speeches as the central bank is in its so-called blackout period ahead of its June 12-13 meeting.
See:MarketWatch's economic calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
Which stocks are in focus?
Among the best performers on Wall Street were retail stocks. Shares of Target Corporation (TGT) rose 4.6%, Kohl's Corp(KSS) rose 3%, while Macy's Inc.(M) and Nordstrom Inc.(JWN) added more than 2.5% each.
Amazon.com Inc. stock (AMZN) rose 0.8% and headed toward a sixth straight record close, lifting its market capitalization above $800 billion (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amazons-market-cap-tops-800-billion-as-stock-surges-toward-6th-straight-record-2018-06-04) intraday, making it the just the second U.S. company to top that level, behind Apple Inc. (AAPL).
Shares of Apple Inc. (AAPL) rose 1.4% ahead of the kickoff of the company's annual Worldwide Developer Conference. The gain is atypical given that the first day of the conference has often been a dud (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-is-how-apples-stock-traded-around-previous-wwdcs-2018-06-04) for Apple shares in the past, according to BTIG.
See:If Apple makes big news at WWDC, that would be big news (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/if-apple-makes-big-news-at-its-developers-conference-next-week-it-would-be-big-news-2018-06-01)
Facebook Inc.(FB) shares were off 0.7%. The New York Times reported that the social media company made agreements with at least 60 makers (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-made-deals-with-device-makers-that-gave-them-access-to-users-information-nyt-2018-06-04) of phones and other devices that gave them access to the personal information of users' friends without their consent. Facebook said it disagreed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/facebook-responds-to-nyt-story-on-data-sharing-says-we-disagree-with-issues-raised-2018-06-04) with the issues raised.
Shares of Microsoft Corp.(MSFT) rose 0.5% after the software giant said it had agreed to buy software-developer platform Github (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/microsoft-to-buy-github-for-75-billion-in-stock-2018-06-04) for $7.5 billion.
Advanced Micro Devices Inc.(AMD) rose 1.6% after surging 4.9% to end at a 10-month high on Friday following a favorable analyst note (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amds-stock-surges-to-9-month-high-after-analyst-price-hike-cisco-adoption-2018-06-01).
Nektar Therapeutics Inc.(NKTR) shares plunged 39% after "underwhelming" results from phase 1/2 clnical trials of its cancer drugs in combination with Bristol-Myers Squibb's cancer drug Opdivo. Shares of Bristol-Myers Squibb(BMY) fell 6%.
What are other markets doing?
Asian stocks closed mostly higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-rally-with-toyota-and-sony-boosting-nikkei-2018-06-03), as traders there got their first chance to react to the upbeat U.S. jobs data from Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 index ended 1.4% higher, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index climbed 1.6%.
Europe traded higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-as-ma-cheer-replaces-political-fears-2018-06-04), setting the Stoxx Europe 600 index on track for its highest close since May 25.
Crude oil prices were lower (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-slip-as-investors-wait-for-opec-to-make-a-move-2018-06-04), while gold hovered near unchanged (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/gold-churns-below-1300-even-as-dollar-nicked-2018-06-04). The ICE U.S. Dollar Index fell 0.1% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dollar-slumps-as-us-trade-policies-rattle-investors-2018-06-04) to 94.077.
